tossups.text: One component of these structures can be repaired using Vortok coils. It's not related to soil, but the Winkler model can be used to analyze the load on these structures, which are protected from deformation by stressing. Historically, these objects had a "bullhead," Vignoles, or Barlow shape. Pandrol develops fasteners used on these objects. Different objects located on top of these structures can display hunting oscillations. These non-racetrack structures are often canted to reduce the radius required for turns, which results in a difference in crosslevel. The ties and sleepers that connect these structures lie on ballast. Four feet, eight and a half inches is the standard distance, or gauge, between these structures. For 10 points, the rolling stock of Norfolk Southern runs on what long metal structures?

This object experiences the Chandler wobble. One observation of this object can be explained using the "Zipper rift" hypothesis, which is currently believed to be as a result of passing the Pasteur point. This body was used by the Juno spacecraft as its final gravitational slingshot. One region in this body alternates between regions of shale and chert and regions of hematite and magnetite and are its banded iron formations. The Alvarez hypothesis includes an explanation of iridium deposits around this body. Density gradients in one part of this object are responsible for its thermohaline circulation. For 10 points, an attempted entry into which object led to the disintegration of NASA's Columbia?

The pathway that produces this molecule recycles a substrate with MTK. A key step in the biosynthesis of this molecule is the formation of an achiral, cyclopropane-substituted amino acid. The response to this molecule is downregulated by a member of the raf family called CTR1. Regulation of ACC synthase is key to a pathway that ends in the synthesis of this molecule, which is named for Yang. This molecule stimulates exaggeration of the apical hook as part of the "triple response." This molecule diffuses in the pericycle and inhibits the transport of IAA. In the absence of auxin, the abscission zone becomes sensitive to this molecule, resulting in plants shedding dead leaves. This hormone is the reason that one rotten apple spoils the bunch. For 10 points, name this gaseous plant hormone that promotes fruit ripening.

The rate of this process is regulated by a 52-residue membrane protein called phospholamban. An irregularity in this process called torsades de pointes(tor-SAHD de PWANNT) is treated by digoxin (dye-GOX-in). Two steps of this process are oddly described as "isovolumic" rather than "isovolumetric." The phases of this process are divided into points labelled P, Q, R, S, and T on a diagram where each square represents 40 milliseconds by 0.1 millivolts. Signals during this process are transmitted through the bundle branches to the Purkinje (pur-KIN-jee) fibers. This process is regulated by the sinoatrial node and is normally divided into systolic and diastolic phases. It occurs too quickly in tachy·cardia. For 10 points, name this internal process that is regulated by a pacemaker and is measured by taking one's pulse.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on pulse until it is read

tossups.text: This artist depicted George and the Dragon in the first use of a shallow relief style called stiacciato. According to Vasari, this artist shouted "Speak, damn you!" at a statue of Habakkuk nicknamed for its pumpkin-like head, Zuccone("zuh-KOH-nay"). This artist's wood artworks include the Santa Croce Crucifix and The Penitent Magdalene. This artist was inspired by a statue of Marcus Aurelius to depict the mercenary Erasmo da Narni in the equestrian statue Gattamelata. In the first freestanding male nude since antiquity, this artist sculpted a boy in a helmet resting one foot on a decapitated head. For 10 points, name this Renaissance sculptor of a bronze David.
acceptableAnswers: Donato di Niccolò di Betto Bardi

tossups.text: While painting Les Demoiselles d'Avignon , Pablo Picasso studied a painting by this artist that features a man dressed in blue raising his arms to the sky. Christ stands flanked by Mary and John the Baptist in a deesis ("DEE-uh-sis") scene at the top of the upper half of a painting by this artist. A landscape by this artist shows the title town on a hill under a stormy, overcast sky. A horizontal row of noblemen watch on as Saints Stephen and Augustine carry Don Gonzalo Ruiz's armored body in the earthly lower half of a painting by this artist. For 10 points, name this Cretan-Spanish artist of View of Toledo and The Burial of the Count of Orgaz .

Elimination reactions of transition metal complexes are almost always this type of reaction. Sodium borohydride, lithium aluminum hydride, and other hydrides are common reagents used to facilitate this type of reaction. The standard hydrogen electrode is used to standardize the cell potential for this type of reaction, which include the conversion of two protons to hydrogen gas. This type of reaction, which includes the electrolysis of a metal cation to produce solid metal, occurs at the cathode of an electrochemical cell. Electrons are gained in--for 10 points--what type of reaction, which are contrasted with oxidation reactions?

Description acceptable. The site of one of these events during Trajan's reign, known as "Vaticana", has been erroneously attributed to Hadrian due to its proximity to his mausoleum. In the Res Gestae, Augustus records one of these events at a site later dedicated to Lucius and Gaius, the Grove of the Caesars. One of these events, addressing a person "from a distant land", is described in an epigram by Martial. Domitian forbade people from changing their clothes at one of these events in a rainstorm, after which some died. According to Suetonius, an emperor responded " Aut nōn " at one of these events when greeted with the only noted use of the phrase " Avē Imperātor, moritūrī tē salūtant ". For its inauguration, Titus held one of these events in the Colosseum and another in Augustus' artificial basin. For 10 points, Claudius used the Fucine Lake to host what type of gladiatorial event?
acceptableAnswers: equivalent before mention by asking “what type of gladiatorial games?”

tossups.text: This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for autoimmune diseases. It plays a key role in the immune system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this vaccine-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The vaccine is a key component of the Immune system, involved in autoimmune diseases.

tossups.text: The song Ma'oz Tzur can be sung during this holiday to celebrate the defeat of Antiochus IV. This holiday is celebrated with an object inscribed with nes, gadol, haya, and sham, and with foods fried in oil, like latke. This holiday includes the spinning of dreidels and the lighting of a namesake type of menorah over this holiday's eight nights. For 10 points, name this Festival of Lights, a Jewish winter holiday.

In this novel, a character leaves a couple with a letter reading "wait and hope." The line "Your death is for my brother, your treasure for his widow" is uttered by Bertuccio as he stabs a man in this novel. The smuggler Jacopo ("YA-ko-po)") waits on an island in this novel. In this novel, Morrel receives a gift signed "Sinbad the Sailor." A character in this novel takes Haydée as a lover. Abbé Faria helps the protagonist of this novel escape from the Château d'If after the latter had been imprisoned by Fernand, Danglars, and Villefort. Edmond Dantés is the title character of, for 10 points, what novel by Alexander Dumas?

In this work, a woman walks through the forest, unable to feel the sunshine, while her daughter basks in it. That same young girl later stays in England at this novel's end, having inherited Chillingworth's money. This novel features an eloquent preacher who delivers a powerful sermon on Election Day. That man, Arthur Dimmesdale, dies in his lover's arms after revealing his adultery through a mark on his chest, matching the title object. For 10 points, name this novel about Hester Prynne, written by Nathaniel Hawthorne.

This document was necessary because of a land dispute mediated by the March Commission that stemmed from a patent the Earl of Warwick gave to Lords Say, Sele, and Brook. This document, which uses the word "combination" instead of "government," was transcribed into the record by Thomas Welles, who later served as governor under it. This government notably omits any reference to the king or crown. It requires voting to be done on slips of paper for all offices of the magistracy, and requires candidates to have served in at least one office in their home parish before they are eligible to be governor. John Haynes led to its creation and became the first governor under this document, most of which was written by Roger Ludlow. Joseph Wadsworth is credited with protecting this document from Edmund Andros. For 10 points, name this document co-authored by Thomas Hooker that was the 1639 charter of government of Connecticut.

This character is forced to manage a garden for two years before escaping his enslavement by the Salé Rovers with the boy Xury. After this character discovers in Lisbon that he has accrued a fortune from Mr. Wells profitably managing his sugar plantation in Brazil, he crosses the Pyrenees, where he is attacked by wolves during a snowstorm. This character convinces a man who worships Benamuckee to call him "master." He meets a parrot named Poll and discovers a mysterious single footprint in a place dubbed "Despair" and found near the mouth of the Orinoco. While on that island, this character fights off cannibals with the help of Friday. For 10 points, name this Alexander Selkirk-inspired stranded sailor, the title character of a Daniel Defoe novel.

The speaker of a poem by this author asks his lover if, prior to meeting, they "snorted... in the Seven Sleepers' den" and later alludes to the Earth's hemispheres. Another poem by this author alludes to erection-inducing angels that set "our flesh upright" and calls the addressee "my America! My new-found-land." In one of this author's poems, two lovers sit next to violets on a river's "pregnant bank." This author of "The Good Morrow" employed the image of a compass in a poem that ends with the lines "Thy firmness makes my circle just, / And makes me end where I begun." He addressed one poem to a being who is "slave to fate, chance, kings, and desperate men" and coined the phrase "No man is an island." For 10 points, name this metaphysical poet of the Holy Sonnets, which includes "Death, be not proud."

In 1999, Kim and Lieber attached these entities to two independent electrodes to prepare the first near-atomic electromechanical system, which operated like a tweezer. Vertically aligned arrays of these entities are often generated using a "tip-growth" or "base-growth" methodology. Another of these entities can be produced in a reaction involving a metal carbonyl catalyst at high pressure called the HiPCO ("hip-COE") method. The perimeter vector of these structures is commonly represented using (m,n) ("m-comma-n") lattice index notation. Depending on how they fold onto themselves, these structures can assume chiral, armchair, or zigzag configurations. In the Russian-doll model, multi-walled examples of these structures comprise many concentric graphene layers. For 10 points, name these cylindrical allotropes of carbon.

Description acceptable.Attendees of this event met at the Capella Hotel on Sentosa Island. One of the clauses in a document agreed upon during this event was a commitment to recover prisoner of war and missing in action remains. This event was partially sparked by fears over the deployment of the Hwasong-15 missile. The planning of this event occurred shortly after the Panmunjom Declaration was made between Moon Jae-In and a neighboring leader. For 10 points, name this June 2018 event where a President and Supreme Leader of traditionally opposed countries met in Singapore in a diplomatic meeting.

An axiomatic formulation of this statement was created by Constantin Caratheodory [CARE-a-THEE-oh-DOOR-ree] and is based on the concept of adiabatic inaccessibility. A corollary of this statement states that the closed line integral of infinitesimal heat exchange divided by temperature is less than or equal to zero. That theorem was formulated by Rudolf Clausius, whose formulation of this law states that heat cannot spontaneously flow from cold to warm regions. A thought experiment that violates this statement involves sorting particles of different speed and is called Maxwell's demon. For ten points, name this law which states that the entropy of a closed system always increases over time.

In one work, this poet writes "On a hack's hired prose, I earn/my exile" and tells himself, "To change your language you must change your life." In another, this poet of "Codicil" calls the central event "a waste of our compassion, as with Spain" and asks "How choose between" the title region "and this English tongue I love...How can I turn from" the title region "and live?" This poet of "A Far Cry from Africa" wrote an epic in which Achille and Hector compete over Helen. For 10 points, name this poet of Omeros, a Caribbean Nobel laureate.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for islets of langerhans. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this insulin-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The insulin is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in islets of langerhans.

parts.text: Name this element, whose medical application comes due to its innermost electron shell's ability to absorb low-energy X-rays. This halogen is also added to table salt to prevent goiter.
Iodine compounds are commonly used for this purpose of enhancing the visibility of internal body parts in medical images. Gadolinium is often used as an agent for this function in MRI.
Another common contrast agent is this element bonded to sulfate. A "meal" of this element is often swallowed when taking an X-ray of the gastrointestinal tract.

bonuses.leadin: This inorganic element is found in diatrizoate, which is often used with an excipient of meglumine or sodium. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this phenomenon, in which domain alignment in the same direction results in a net magnetic moment. It is often seen in metals like nickel and cobalt.

This simple model of ferromagnetism models domains as points on a lattice, with the Hamiltonian consisting of nearest-neighbors that are either aligned or anti-aligned. A formal solution to the two dimensional version of this model was developed by Lars Onsager.

The Curie-Weiss law from which the Curie temperature is obtained is actually an expression for this quantity, which becomes infinite when the Curie temperature is reached. It represents the magnitude of the magnetization in response to an applied field.

bonuses.leadin: This phenomenon vanishes above the Curie temperature when domains lose their alignment and become disordered. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this condition which occurs due to decreased transport of oxygen to various tissues.
Intrinsic factor, which is required for absorption of B12, is secreted by these cells in the stomach, which are also responsible for secreting gastric acid.
Murphy, Minot, and Whipple showed that dogs suffering from anemia improved after they were fed extracts of this organ. This organ also converts lactate to glucose in the Cori cycle.

bonuses.leadin: The pernicious variety of this condition is caused by the decreased absorption of vitamin B12. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify these date structures, which are last in first out and which can be modeled by people standing in a line.
Implementing a queue in real life requires these structures, which is a data type that refers to another value stored somewhere in memory. Dangling ones are annoying to use.
Dangling pointers can be rectified via this procedure, which removes data objects that won't be used by the program anymore. Mark-and-sweep is one method of implementing it.

bonuses.leadin: The A* algorithm uses a special version of these data structures which assign an additional priority measure to data added to them. FTPE:

parts.text: Identify this avant-garde composer fond of micropolyphony, also known for works like the anti-anti-opera, Le Grand Macabre.

"The Devil's Staircase" and "Autumn in Warsaw" are two of 18 pieces in this genre composed by Ligeti between 1985 and 2001. Carl Czerny ("CHAIR-nee") collected his many pieces in this genre in books such as The School of Velocity.

Ligeti's The Future of Music, where he simply wrote the words "Crescendo," "piu forte," and "Silence" on a blackboard is often compared to this composer's 4'33" ("four minutes, thirty-three seconds").

bonuses.leadin: One score by this composer advises percussionists "be sure to wear protective goggles" while performing the instruction to break a bottle onto a crate. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The Tribuna of the Uffizi is by Johan Zoffany, a founding member of this institution alongside many others including Mary Moser and Angelica Kauffman. Joshua Reynolds was appointed the first president of this institution.

In The Tribuna of the Uffizi, curator Pietro Bastianelli shows off this painting to Thomas Patch and others. A spotted white dog lays on the foot of a bed in front of a maid grabbing clothes from a chest in this painting.
The Tribuna of the Uffizi depicts a room in this city's Uffizi museum. This city's artists were patronized by the Medici family and contrasted artistic styles from its rival Venice.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following questions about The Tribuna of the Uffizi, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this process in which an electric current drives a non-spontaneous chemical reaction.
This equation finds the electrode potential for an electrolysis reaction. It states that change in electrode potential is equal to RT over zF times the natural log of the reaction quotient.
This equation is the generalization of the Nernst Equation, as it factors in permeability, multiple ions, and the ratio of concentrations to determine equilibrium potential.

bonuses.leadin: This method is used to produce hydrogen and chlorine gas from a solution of brine. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this two-word Latin principle, which allowed any single member of the Polish nobility to nullify legislation and end the current session.
During the time that the liberum veto was in effect, Poland was in a commonwealth with this other country. Poland and this "grand duchy" established that commonwealth with the 1569 Union of Lublin.

In an earlier bout of self-interest, Polish nobles arranged the 1386 marriage of Queen Jadwiga with this Lithuanian grand duke, who founded a namesake Polish dynasty that reigned until the election of Henry Valois in 1573.

bonuses.leadin: Because of this rule, nothing ever got done in the Sejm. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with cartilage types.
What is the main function of the synovial in the musculoskeletal system?
Name another component of the musculoskeletal system related to cartilage types.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human musculoskeletal system.

parts.text: Name this holiday near the end of the Christian Holy Week. It commemorates the day of Jesus's crucifixion.
Holy Week, which ends Lent, leads up to this important springtime Christian holiday, which celebrates Jesus's resurrection.
The Thursday before Good Friday, which commemorates the Last Supper, is often given this name, which is thought to come from the Latin for "commandment."

bonuses.leadin: In Catholicism, this solemn holiday is a fast day on which no mass is observed. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this character married to a paralyzed aristocrat named Clifford. She later begins an affair with the estate gamekeeper, Oliver Mellors.
Besides writing Lady Chatterley's Lover, this author wrote The Rainbow and described Ursula and Gudrun Brangwen's various relationships in Women in Love.
This D.H. Lawrence novel describes the love triangle between Paul Morel, Miriam Leivers, and Clara Dawes. However, Paul fails to marry either woman and ends up broken-hearted and alone.

bonuses.leadin: She begins a brief affair with the playwright Michaelis at her estate, Wragby. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this play, whose titular object brings Blanche to Elysian Fields.
Identify the author of A Streetcar Named Desire.
Tennessee Williams also wrote this play, in which Brick and Maggie's turbulent marriage almost ruins their inheritance of Big Daddy's property, which Mae and Gooper also vied for.
parts.answer: Cat on a Hot Tin Roof
acceptableAnswers: Cat on a Hot Tin Roof
The Cat on a Hot Tin Roof

parts.text: Name this man impersonated by Grigory Otrepiev, who promised to convert Russia to Catholicism after marrying a Polish princess.
Dmitry was impersonated by three usurpers during this period, which ended when Michael I came to power and saw Russia invaded by Poland, Sweden, and the Tatars.

The succession crisis that culminated in the Time of Troubles began after this ruler murdered his son, Ivan, leaving only the mentally ill Fedor as his heir. This ruler's Russian nickname, Grozny, can be more accurately translated as "awe-inspiring".

bonuses.leadin: An official investigation conducted by Vasily Shuisky concluded that instead of being murdered, this person stabbed himself in the throat after he had a seizure while playing a spear-throwing game. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this short story, whose title quantity can be decreased using a Nefastis machine in a different work.
In this other work by the author of Entropy, Oedipa Maas meets the inventor of the Nefastis machine while on her search to understand the meaning of the Trystero.
Entropy and The Crying of Lot 49 were both written by this reclusive, American author of Gravity's Rainbow.

bonuses.leadin: In this short story, Castillo worries about cosmic heat-death while trying to nurse a bird back to life and Meatball throws a party that devolves into chaos. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this novel in which the protagonist has an affair with the Lebanese millionaire Wani. This novel by Alan Hollinghurst follows the gay man Nick Guest in 1980s Britain.

"To Whom Do You Beautifully Belong?" is a quote by this author, whom Nick is writing his thesis on. Nick is working on a screenplay of The Spoils of Poynton, a novel by this author of The Turn of the Screw.

The Line of Beauty references a scene in which this character is surprised to see her husband seated while Madame Merle is standing. This Henry James character is the protagonist of The Portrait of a Lady.

bonuses.leadin: In this novel, whose sections include one titled "To Whom Do You Beautifully Belong?," the protagonist says of an author that "we wouldn't have realized... that he'd seen right through us." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this value that can be solved for by integrating over the Mayer f-function. It describes deviation from the ideal gas law due to pairwise potential.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on “virial” as that is a different quantity

parts.text: The second virial coefficient goes to zero at a temperature named for this man. According to this man's law, pressure and volume are inversely proportional under constant temperature for an ideal gas.

For the van der Waals equation of state, the second virial coefficient can be expressed in terms of a and b. This cubic equation of state further modifies the a and b parameters and predicts a critical compressibility factor of one-third.

parts.text: Name this leader of the Nationalist Party. This Generalissimo was succeeded by King Juan Carlos I as head of state.
In the Spanish Civil War, this country, along with the Soviet Union, supported the Republicans. Then led by Cardenas, this country has traditionally been ruled by the PRI party.
Franco was a member of this Fascist party founded by Jose Antonio Primo de Rivera. Under his oversight, it merged with the monarchist Carlists.

parts.text: Name this double-membraned organelle that generates a majority of a cell's energy. This organelle is nicknamed the "powerhouse of the cell."
Mitochondria break down glucose in order to drive oxidative phosphorylation and create this compound, the cell's chemical energy "currency."
This theory states that mitochondria were originally bacteria that were absorbed by other cells, explaining the origin of eukaryotic cells from prokaryotic cells.

bonuses.leadin: This organelle's inner membrane is made up of numerous folds called cristae. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The metafictional novel If on a winter's night a traveler, a book about you, the reader, attempting to read the metafictional novel If on a winter's night a traveler, was written by this author.
This English author wrote the metafictional novel Atonement, in which Briony Tallis writes the metafictional novel Atonement about Briony Tallis writing the metafictional novel Atonement.
Metafictional literature is generally associated with this style of experimental literature to which both If on a winter's night a traveler and Atonement belong.
